feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the content shows real ownership of platforms, governance, analytics, and multimedia. It reads professionally, but impact would improve with tighter formatting, more quantified outcomes, and a few style/grammar fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and career progression consistently support a digital platform/communications leadership profile.  
- Strong credibility: long tenure at NACo, promotion history, major platform scope (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers), and relevant technical stack all reinforce expertise.  
- Good breadth with relevance: combines strategy, CMS/platform delivery, analytics, governance, AI search, and multimedia in a way that fits modern communications leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Improve structure and scannability: the “footer” projects section feels misplaced, and there is some duplication across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT. Consolidate to reduce repetition.  
- Add sharper outcomes: several bullets describe responsibilities well but need stronger results (e.g., % efficiency gains, engagement growth, adoption improvements, campaign performance).  
- Fix style consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “scripting, and production” also has an unnecessary comma; capitalization is inconsistent in “Coleman DAVIS”; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak filler versus stronger academic detail or omission.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and public-sector focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value statement plus one scope statement; reduce the long list of functions.
- Add 1–2 concrete signals of scale or leadership from recent roles (for example, enterprise web modernization, 10,000+ pages, 50+ publishers, 3.5M annual page views).
- Replace “Leads” with “Led” or “Has led” for tense consistency, unless you want a deliberately present-tense branding style.
- Possible rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing web platforms, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Has led enterprise Drupal migrations, editorial and publishing systems, analytics infrastructure, multimedia production, and emerging AI-enabled search experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The capability list closely duplicates Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and making categories slightly more distinctive will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and simplify wording: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Replace broad items with sharper, higher-value terms: “Cross-channel communications operations” or “Digital communications operations” instead of “Multi-channel communications operations.”
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • Cross-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Keep “and” vs “&” consistent across the section and CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences,” “workflow automation,” analytics, governance, and multimedia already appear in Topline Skills and the header.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” in Topline Skills.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently repeats several themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening the wording and adding clearer outcomes or scope where possible would make it feel more distinct and higher impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item consistently with action + platform/scope + purpose/outcome.
- Tighten phrasing: e.g., “Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat.”
- Replace generic terms like “improve discovery” or “designed for continued campaign growth” with sharper outcomes if available: user adoption, scalability, engagement, launch context, or audience served.
- Standardize style and punctuation: use “10 x 20-foot” (not “10×20-foot”) and keep parallel verbs across all entries.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with recent NACo roles; keep this section more project-specific than responsibility-based.
- “Built/Developed” repeats heavily; vary verbs or use a cleaner noun-led project format.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten it around strategic outcomes and differentiate it from the prior NACo staff roles by emphasizing advisory/consulting scope and new initiatives.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client value: “Advise the National Association of Counties on enterprise digital strategy, content operations, campaign platforms, and web modernization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 sharper points focused on consulting impact: digital systems/workflows/analytics; Drupal campaign builds; governance across channels; AI-enabled search leadership.
- Use stronger outcome-oriented phrasing: “Designed,” “Led,” “Implemented,” “Standardized,” “Improved.” Add metrics if possible (site traffic, toolkit downloads, publishing speed, search success, stakeholder adoption).
- Example rewrite: “Lead digital strategy and platform consulting for NACo, improving content operations, analytics, Drupal campaign delivery, cross-channel governance, and AI-enabled search discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording overlaps heavily with the 2022–2024 Director role on governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement.
- Microsites and AI search also duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and reserve project specifics for the project section.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be even stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget, leading enterprise modernization of core communications platforms.”
- Prioritize the website transformation first and make it outcome-led: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten channel bullet and add measurable outcomes if available (growth, engagement, open rates, production volume), rather than “reaching tens of thousands” / “serving thousands.”
- Combine governance/analytics into one operational-improvement bullet if space is tight, emphasizing decision-making, standards, and cross-team efficiency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Email/social/video management overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and modernization.
- Video-program expansion may duplicate footer projects and earlier NACo bullets unless framed as “built first in-house studio.”

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Tighten it around what changed under your ownership: newsletter operations, advocacy video, and cross-team editorial systems.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day multi-channel digital communications operations across web, email, social and video for NACo’s advocacy and member communications.”
- Make bullets more outcome-led: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders, improving consistency and cadence of member communications.”
- Sharpen the video bullet: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing with systems language: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led digital communications across web, email, social media and video” is too close to the Director of Digital Media entry.
- “Helped improve workflows” overlaps with both earlier team-building and later governance bullets; make this role specifically about editorial coordination.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level leadership areas not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, outcome-oriented skill labels tied to recent work:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance and cross-team publishing operations
- Multi-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Audience-centered content strategy for advocacy and member engagement
- Consider dropping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” unless messaging itself is a target role requirement; “content strategy” is stronger and broader.
- Keep wording parallel and concise; avoid nouns that repeat “systems,” “governance,” and “communications” without adding specificity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also repeats both Core Competencies and multiple recent NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize highest-value, recent capabilities tied to enterprise web modernization and delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from platform inventory to capability-led phrasing; lead with the most marketable, recent strengths.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based content systems • SharePoint and Power Pages • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put Drupal first and group WordPress later or remove it if it is not central to recent roles.
- If space allows, replace one generic term with an outcome-oriented qualifier, e.g., “enterprise CMS modernization” or “scalable content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep this version strategic/high-level and leave full tool inventory there.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating the exact phrasing if possible.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. Make this more outcome-oriented and leadership-level.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + decision impact, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” rather than separate bullets if space is tight.
- Replace generic phrases with stronger wording: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive dashboarding and leadership reporting” instead of “Leadership reporting.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy and optimization • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive dashboarding and performance reporting • SEO, UX and conversion analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave the full tool inventory there.
- “Performance analysis” may overlap with broader “digital strategy” language elsewhere unless tied to analytics outcomes.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Make it more senior, outcomes-oriented, and tied to recent leadership-level multimedia work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio Operations & Event Delivery**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level phrasing: **Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ camera and multi-camera workflows • Virtual event production**
- If space allows, add one impact cue rather than only tools: **Built and led in-house multimedia capabilities supporting advocacy programming, recurring video content and live events**
- Avoid listing “editing” separately unless paired with a tool or outcome; it reads junior compared with the rest of the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” / “livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies and Technical + IT.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with work experience bullets about studio/event capacity; keep this skills item concise, not narrative.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a bare inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since Drupal is the strongest and most recent platform in the experience section, this item should emphasize depth/order rather than repeat generic CMS names.

Suggested edit
- Reorder by demonstrated strength and recency: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider “Drupal (enterprise migration, modular microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If formatting allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Keep platform names only; avoid mixing in broader terms like “CMS modernization” here since that belongs in competencies.
- If space is tight, drop GitHub Pages unless it is materially relevant to target roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms.
- Consider merging both into one stronger platform-focused entry to reduce repetition.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical range, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior digital leader, emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more senior and specific, e.g. “Front-End Development & Technical Implementation.”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”
- Consider grouping by function for readability: “Front-end: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Integration/ops: API integrations, GTM, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”
- If space allows, swap one generic item for evidence of use in recent roles, e.g. “JavaScript-based front-end customization” or “deployment/workflow automation,” but avoid adding tools not supported elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under Analytics/Optimization unless implementation is a core selling point.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and signal level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and keep only strongest, most relevant tools: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana | Collaboration: Slack, Teams”
- Remove lower-value/general tools unless heavily used in recent roles: Basecamp, Trello
- If accurate, add light proficiency/context wording in the title or line: “Automation & Workflow Systems (build/admin)” or “Automation, PM & Collaboration Tools”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same language elsewhere.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep only if they support a broader systems/operations narrative.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, especially given the recent email leadership in NACo roles, but it reads as a bare vendor list. Strengthen it by signaling level of use and aligning it to enterprise communications systems rather than repeating channel ownership already covered in experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (campaign operations, newsletter distribution, audience engagement workflows)**
- If accurate, add scope/level: **Enterprise email and member communications platforms supporting newsletter, campaign and stakeholder engagement programs**
- Keep only the strongest/current tools; order by recency/relevance, with Dynamics 365 first.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; avoid adding outcome claims here unless they are platform-specific.
- “Engagement” may blur with social/web responsibilities already covered elsewhere; keep this item tightly focused on email/member communications systems.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool set, but this item is too generic and largely repeats the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills. Use it to sharpen technical specificity and emphasize implementation/measurement rather than broad concepts.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with more concrete capabilities: “GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • Experimentation/A/B testing • KPI dashboard development”
- Consider ordering by strongest/recent tools first based on recent roles: “GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio …”
- If space allows, add one higher-value technical qualifier instead of “Dashboarding,” e.g. “reporting architecture” or “analytics implementation”
- If this section supports ATS, keep naming consistent with work history wording: “GA4,” “Microsoft Clarity,” “Power BI,” “Looker Studio,” “BigQuery”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with Topline Skills [3]; consider trimming one or making this version more tool-only.
- “SEO” and “A/B testing” are broad skill areas, not tools; they may fit better in competencies than Technical + IT.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles on workflows, video, and digital operations. Make it more foundational and specific to this earlier stage.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize team-building and first-generation digital infrastructure: “Promoted through two roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize early workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add clearer scope and outputs: “Supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and recurring video updates; coordinated day-to-day digital publishing and multimedia delivery.”
- Tighten the management point: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised one digital media associate,” if accurate.
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos, audience growth, publishing volume, or website/project scale.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “strengthening workflows” overlaps with the 2018–2024 roles; frame this as early-stage setup rather than ongoing operational leadership.
- “weekly video updates” is repeated in the next role; distinguish this as launching or initially producing the series.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch and frame the rest as cross-functional program support rather than broad “digital content production.”

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the clearest achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program teams; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “contributed to digital content production” with a more specific support function, e.g., “developed multimedia and digital content assets for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audiences served, teams supported, or how the podcast/content supported advocacy, member engagement, or organizational visibility.
- Keep this entry concise since later roles show the fuller digital leadership progression.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with the 2015–2024 NACo roles; avoid repeating broad multimedia language.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here, since later entries more credibly show management and enterprise ownership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, and keep workflow/production capabilities in experience or topline skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Creative Software**
- Replace with: **Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator**
